name: Lytzen IT / NetNordic AAL-DC1 Aalborg
notes: Inflect lists AAL-DC1 at 1 Langagervej, Aalborg, operated by NetNordic with reported 1.5 MW power; NetNordic announced acquisition of Lytzen IT in 2022, including Aalborg/Hjorring/Copenhagen locations.

name: Green DC heat-reuse demonstration at Aalborg University
developer: Energy Cluster Denmark / Aalborg University / Heatflow / R&R Consult
notes: Innovation project named Green DC seeks CO2-neutral server cooling and surplus heat delivery to district heating/local buildings; recorded as data-center-related project activity rather than a hyperscale campus.

name: Apple Foulum/Viborg Data Center
notes: Apple source states Esbjerg wind power supports Apple's data center in Viborg; DDI reported Apple planned to expand the Viborg data center and capture excess heat; datacenters.com states the facility opened in 2020.

name: Kolo DK2 Aarhus
notes: Operator page lists DK2 Aarhus on Silkeborgvej in central Aarhus with N+N power redundancy and 100% renewable energy.

name: Kolo DK1 Skanderborg
notes: Operator page lists DK1 Skanderborg near Aarhus as a Tier 3-ready colocation data center with N+N redundancy, 1.25 PUE, renewable power and high-density cabinet support.

name: Kolo DK4 Viby J
notes: Operator page lists DK4 in Viby J near Aarhus, powered by 100% Danish renewable energy and positioned for colocation workloads.

name: Google Fredericia Data Center
notes: Google location page says the Fredericia hyperscale data centre opened in 2020; Google announced groundbreaking in 2018 for its first Denmark data center.

name: Meta Odense Data Center
notes: Meta lists Odense with 10 billion+ DKK investment and 2017 groundbreaking; Ramboll states the Odense heat-reuse installation supplies about 45 MW of heat to district heating.

name: Bulk DK01 Esbjerg Campus
notes: Bulk operator page lists DK01 in Esbjerg; DCD/Baxtel report the campus opened in 2019 with capacity to initially support 20 MW across 50,000 sqm.

name: Prime Data Centers Esbjerg AI-ready campus
developer: Prime Data Centers / Brunswick Real Estate
notes: Prime announced an Esbjerg campus with first phase totaling 160 MW IT capacity and potential expansion to 550 MW IT, subject to demand and permitting.

name: atNorth DEN02 Varde Mega Site
notes: atNorth operator page lists a 171-hectare Varde greenfield campus with 500 MW campus power capacity for colocation and build-to-suit; DCD earlier reported the Olgod/Varde project as a 250 MW plan expected by end-2026.

name: Thylander Data Centers Esbjerg hyperscale project
notes: DCD reported Thylander plans a fully Danish developed, operated, and owned hyperscale data center in Esbjerg; article states 100 MW, launch target 2026, initial 10-20 MW and expansion potential to 200 MW.

name: University of Southern Denmark Sonderborg AI supercomputer data center
developer: University of Southern Denmark / Danfoss / HPE
notes: Danfoss announced the Danish AI/supercomputing data center with SDU and HPE; DCD later reported the Sonderborg system had been brought online using HPE AI Mod POD modular data center technology.

name: Apple Kassoe/Aabenraa second Denmark data center
notes: Apple canceled its planned second Danish data center at Kasso/Aabenraa in June 2019 and put the 285-hectare site up for sale; included as rejected historical project activity.

name: Microsoft Denmark East - Hoje Taastrup campus
notes: Microsoft announced opening of Denmark East on 2026-03-26 with campuses in Hoje Taastrup, Koge, and Roskilde; local Microsoft page confirms Hoje Taastrup was the third Danish datacenter construction start.

name: atNorth DEN01 Copenhagen metro site
notes: atNorth lists DEN01 in Ballerup/greater Copenhagen; first phase went live in Q4 2025 and provides 30 MW for high-density workloads with heat reuse.

name: STACK Infrastructure COP02 Copenhagen/Taastrup campus
notes: STACK operator page states COP02 in Copenhagen/Taastrup is designed for 72 MW critical capacity across two buildings, one 48 MW and one 24 MW.

name: Digital Realty Copenhagen Campus
notes: Digital Realty operator pages list four Copenhagen data centers, including Ballerup CPH2 and CPH3, with 251,500 sq ft / 23,300 sq m total colocation space in the metro.

name: Kolo DK5 Copenhagen
notes: Kolo operator page lists DK5 Copenhagen as a centrally located retrofit colocation data center optimized for compute-intensive workloads, liquid-cooled high-density racks and ultra-low-latency connectivity.

name: Microsoft Denmark East - Koge and Roskilde campuses
notes: Microsoft announced Denmark East with campuses in Koge and Roskilde on Zealand; DCD reported second-phase construction activity at Koge around the same launch period.

name: GARBE Data Centers Business Park Falster AI campus
notes: Guldborgsund Municipality announced a conditional land sale at Business Park Falster for GARBE's AI data center campus; official/local source states expected 350 MW capacity and DCD reports up to DKK 20bn investment on 35 hectares.
